A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVNet research work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–E are readable, and visual inspection supports comparison of equations, figures, and tables. Some reporting inconsistencies limit individual numerical comparisons but do not prevent comparison of the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-alignment, shape-bias, image-classification, robustness, ablation, and EfficientNet generalization results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original results across the retained evaluations, with additional component studies, adversarial controls, CORnet-Z experiments, and inference-ensembling analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces the parameterized Naka–Rushton light-adaptation function with (x − xbar)/xbar, substantively changing a central front-end computation. v2 also introduces an LGN–V2 skip-connection variant and multiple-pass activation-aggregation procedures in Appendices D.3 and E.3. The overall SubcorticalBlock–VOneBlock architecture remains.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-C, the same five domain-shift datasets, cue-conflict images, BrainScore benchmarks, and grating-based response evaluations. Additional architectures, ablations, and inference procedures reuse this coverage. The added empirical V1 curves illustrate published responses rather than introduce a new evaluation dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds VOneResNet50+PRIME to the main robustness comparison in Table 5 and CORnet-Z as a base-model comparator in Appendix D.2. The existing ResNet50, VOneResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, PRIME-trained ResNet50, and adversarial-training comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: PGD changes from 16 to 64 iterations, step size from budget/8 to budget/32, and gradient samples from 32 to 10. New variant and back-end adversarial evaluations use six attacks. Appendix E also changes the reported EfficientNet optimizer from SGD to RMSProp and maximum learning rate from 0.1 to 0.256. Exact stronger L2 budgets remain unresolved: v2 Table 4 lists 2.4 and 9.6, while its prose retains 1.2 and 2.4.

E4.justification: The four original component ablations expand to include P-cell and VOneBlock removal and an LGN–V2 connection variant, with new neural-alignment and adversarial analyses (Table 6 and Appendix D.1). v2 adds PGD-iteration convergence controls, revises gradient-sampling sensitivity tests, extends back-end generalization, and tests ensemble size and aggregation location.

E5.justification: Main adversarial and aggregate tables change their reported seed counts from two to three. Table 5 newly supplies mean±SD for ResNet50+PRIME, previously shown without uncertainty. Mean±SD remains the established reporting practice; no confidence intervals or significance-testing framework is added.

E6.justification: Results change throughout the paper. Table 1 reports EVResNet50 V1 predictivity changing from 0.379 to 0.364, response-property alignment from 0.808 to 0.826, and shape bias from 46.3% to 48.9%; Table 2 clean accuracy changes from 71.7% to 70.4%. Under the respective attack protocols, EVNet/VOneNet adversarial means change from 25.9/26.6% to 28.3/26.1%, reversing their ranking. Numerous variant, back-end, and ensemble results are added. These are revised-method or revised-protocol results, not controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 2 substantively revises the mathematical definition of light adaptation and removes its exponent and centering-bias parameters. The DoG and contrast-normalization definitions, push-pull identity and assumptions, and Bayesian tuning objective remain. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction removes explicit claims of improved V1 predictivity and maintained similar clean accuracy, and highlights back-end generalization. The abstract updates the reported robustness margins from 8.5% to 9.3% and from 7.3% to 6.2% with PRIME. The central contributions of biologically constrained front-ends, improved alignment and robustness, and complementary augmentation gains remain.

C2.justification: The expanded ablations substantially revise component interpretations: M cells and contrast normalization support neural alignment despite limited robustness effects, while removing VOneBlock largely preserves aggregate robustness. v2 adds explanations involving filtering, local competition, and ensemble suppression of useful stochasticity. It removes the earlier interpretation of reduced mean adversarial robustness and newly discusses light-adaptation instability without contrast normalization and possible task-driven front-end fine-tuning.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-model-weights link, optimized parameters and kernel sizes in Table E2, per-variant calibration details, and explicit skip-connection and contrast-normalization-ablation implementations. Appendix A also documents additional back-end integration details. These substantially extend v1's search bounds and training information, although Table E2 reports a P-cell optimum of −0.12 outside its stated search interval.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds a focused discussion of subcortical ideas in edge detection, Retinex, multiscale representations, and modern CNNs. The discussion adds the Bitter Lesson and neural-scaling literature and sharpens positioning around separate P/M pathways. The principal VOneNet-centered research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are targeted edits to the abstract, contributions, results, and discussion; Section 3.4 is refocused on EVNet variants, and Appendices B and E gain more explicit subsections. Affiliations, contact information, and the conference header change. The overall organization and substantial portions of the explanatory prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6 and figures for empirical V1 curves, PGD convergence, and inference ensembling. The four-category corruption plot becomes a 15-corruption display including PRIME variants. Figure 1's light-adaptation schematic is redrawn, tuning plots are revised, and appendix tables expand to display additional variants, architectures, and optimized parameters.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence that was limited in v1: PGD convergence controls better support the adversarial evaluation, the VOneNet+PRIME comparator tests the incremental contribution more directly, and expanded ablations distinguish contributors to neural alignment and robustness. Parameter disclosures and the code/weights link improve reproducibility information, while narrowed claims acknowledge performance tradeoffs. These gains outweigh unresolved reporting problems, particularly the conflicting L2 budgets and the out-of-range optimum in Table E2.
